title: PhylogenyPro: a browser-based platform for molecular phylogenetics, from the alignment to the dated tree
description:
PhylogenyPro is a self-contained web application that carries a set of sequences through a whole phylogenetic study in the browser, with no installation and no server-side computation. It reads FASTA, PHYLIP, NEXUS, Clustal, MEGA and GenBank files and morphological matrices, aligns them with a progressive aligner that can work on codons, and lets the alignment be trimmed and edited by hand. Each partition declares its genome — chloroplast, mitochondrion, nuclear ribosomal or low-copy nuclear — and that declaration is carried into every later step. It selects among 56 DNA models, twelve empirical amino-acid matrices and Mk/Mkv for morphology by AIC, AICc and BIC, and finds partition schemes by greedy merging; infers trees by parsimony, distance methods, maximum likelihood with NNI and SPR search, and Metropolis-coupled Bayesian MCMC, both of the last two running in Web Workers; measures support by bootstrap, ultrafast bootstrap, SH-aLRT, aBayes and posterior probabilities, and compares topologies with the KH, SH and AU tests. It then tests the molecular clock, dates the tree by least squares, penalised likelihood or a relaxed clock with fossil calibrations on the geological time scale; fits models of diversification; reconstructs continuous and discrete ancestral characters with stochastic mapping, BM/OU/EB, independent contrasts, PGLS, Blomberg's K and Pagel's lambda; reconstructs ancestral areas with DEC, DIVALIKE and BAYAREALIKE with and without founder-event speciation; and compares trees by five distances, concordance factors, quartets, split networks and ABBA-BABA.

Throughout, an interpretation guide places each computed number on its own scale, and a calibration assistant turns a fossil, a geological event or a known rate into a prior and says what it means in years. It ends in a tree studio with pictures of the OTUs and clades and a cut into k groups, a figure studio that restyles every figure in the twelve blocks at once, figures at any resolution, a methods section written from what was actually run, and a reproducible package the program writes itself.

Every block is checked against an independent implementation in R: 1116 unit tests and 258 numerical agreements with ape, phangorn, geiger, phytools, nlme, BioGeoBEARS and xml2, with no mismatch. The archive includes simulated example data sets and a user manual in Spanish (HTML and PDF, 112 pages).
